title: Heap Greedy Settle-Up versus the Exact Optimum
instructions: In `heap_settle.py` implement the greedy `settle_heap` with two `heapq` heaps, the exact `min_transfers_exact` solver (bitmask DP over zero-sum groups) and the `apply_transfers` oracle. The greedy plan must be deterministic and independent of insertion order, and you should be able to explain what it guarantees and what it does not.

evidence.label: Pairs the largest debtor with the largest creditor and pushes remainders back
Ignores zero balances and returns [] for empty input
Rejects balances that do not sum to zero (ValueError) and non-int balances (TypeError)
Produces the same plan whatever the insertion order
Plans clear all balances, go debtor to creditor, and use at most n-1 transfers
Exact solver returns the true minimum on known cases and rejects more than 16 balances
Greedy never beats the exact optimum and is sometimes strictly worse
apply_transfers returns the remaining non-zero balances
Ties go to the alphabetically smallest user
Exact solver ignores zero balances and finds disjoint zero-sum groups
